analyst_view.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points under Enzo Maresca, but they have not won in the Premier League for over a month and lost 3-1 at Nottingham Forest. Napoli, under Massimiliano Allegri, are 27th on 3 points after a 4-1 defeat at Porto. Napoli's injury list is shrinking: Neres, Spinazzola and Favasuli are back, and Di Lorenzo and Badiashile could return for this game. Lobotka, Buongiorno and goalkeeper Meret are still out, and Rafa Marín is banned, which the numbers already count. City are without Semenyo (knee, back around December), while Guehi, Khusanov and Matheus Nunes were doubts before the weekend. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and already count Napoli's leaky recent defending (+3% City) and Marín's ban. Napoli getting Di Lorenzo and Badiashile back would tighten them, but City's own defensive doubts (Guehi, Khusanov) cut the other way. With signals on both sides, I stay at 3.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with City around 6.5, and already add about 7% for how many corners Napoli have been conceding. An Allegri side that sits deep tends to concede corners, but that is already part of their record. I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, with Napoli's slightly higher recent count counted (+7%). Nobody on either side is in a known ban risk that changes things, and no referee is named. I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots and already add about 15% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Defenders returning for Napoli could reduce that a little, but City's attack is unchanged apart from Semenyo, who has been out since October. I stay at 29.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, including City's recent boost (+8%). There is no clear new news on either side's forwards; De Bruyne may have his minutes managed. I stay at 10.6.
